arguments.command:
printf "1) 🐍 Python project
2) 🐑 Node.js project
3) 🐏 Bash script

" && read -rp "Choose (1-3): " choice && read -rp "Project name: " name && tput cuu 1 && mkdir -p "$name" && if [ "$choice" = "1" ]; then termy_say "Creating Python project" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "
" && touch "$name/main.py" "$name/requirements.txt" && echo "# $name" > "$name/README.md" && echo "🚀 ✅ Python project created"; elif [ "$choice" = "2" ]; then termy_say "Creating Node project" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "
" && cd "$name" && npm init -y > /dev/null && touch "index.js" && cd .. && echo "🚀 ✅ Node.js project created"; elif [ "$choice" = "3" ]; then termy_say "Creating Bash script" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "
" && cat > "$name/script.sh" << 'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
echo "Script initialized"
EOF
 chmod +x "$name/script.sh" && echo "🚀 ✅ Bash script created"; else printf "
Invalid option
"; fi && printf ""
arguments.explanation: Provides a POSIX-compliant interactive menu to scaffold a basic template structure for Python, Node.js, or Bash projects while issuing specific audio announcements.
arguments.goal: Scaffold a new project structure based on template selection

input: serve the contents of this folder

arguments.command: read -p "🌐 Port (default 8000): " port && port=${port:-8000} && tput cuu 1 && termy_say "Starting Python HTTP server on port $port" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "\r\n" && echo "Serving at http://localhost:$port (Ctrl+C to stop)" && python3 -m http.server "$port" && printf ""
arguments.explanation: Prompts for a port number and starts a basic Python HTTP server in the current directory to share files.
arguments.goal: Start a local Python HTTP server

arguments.command: read -p "📁 Venv name (default: venv): " name && name=${name:-venv} && tput cuu 1 && termy_say "Creating Python virtual environment" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "\r\n" && python3 -m venv "$name" && echo -e "✅ Created venv '\033[1m$name\033[22m'. Activate with: source $name/bin/activate" && printf ""
arguments.explanation: Prompts for a virtual environment name, creates it using python3 -m venv, and provides the activation command.

arguments.command:
tput cuu 1 && termy_say "Please enter the python script path" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "
🐍 Python script path: " && read -r script && if [ -f "$script" ]; then if command -v python3 > /dev/null 2>&1; then python3 "$script" && printf "
" && termy_say "Script executed successfully" > /dev/null 2>&1; elif command -v python > /dev/null 2>&1; then python "$script" && printf "
" && termy_say "Script executed successfully" > /dev/null 2>&1; else termy_say "Python not found, do you want to activate the virtual environment" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "
⛔ Python not found. Activate venv? y/n: " && read -r ans && case "$ans" in [yY]*) printf "
" && if command -v locate_and_activate_venv > /dev/null 2>&1; then locate_and_activate_venv; else activate_venv; fi ;; *) printf "
⛔ Operation cancelled.
" ;; esac; fi; else printf "
⛔ Script file does not exist.
" && termy_say "File not found" > /dev/null 2>&1; fi
arguments.explanation: Runs a Python script using python3 or python, or prompts to activate the virtual environment if missing.

arguments.command: tput cuu 1 && termy_say "Creating a new environment file" > /dev/null 2>&1 && printf "\r\n" && create_env_file && printf "\n" && termy_say "Environment file created successfully" > /dev/null 2>&1
arguments.explanation: Creates a new .env file in the current directory.
Adds or updates an entry in the existing .env file in the current directory.
Displays a list of keys from the .env file and removes the selected one.
